summary: This Docusaurus plugin creates plain-Markdown mirrors of blog posts and builds searchable indexes (llms.txt files) so readers and LLMs can access article content without needing React or the interactive components in the HTML version. It finds all published posts, converts MDX to Markdown, writes the mirrors next to their URLs, and generates a site-wide index plus per-series bundles—handling multiple locales by preferring translated versions when they exist.

explanations.32: fs.readdirSync() returns file/folder entries from a directory, and withFileTypes: true means each entry has an .isDirectory() method so we can tell files apart from folders.
explanations.35: The three dots (...) spread operator unpacks the array returned by the recursive findPosts() call and adds each item individually to the found array, flattening nested results.
explanations.49: This regex finds a lowercase letter or digit followed immediately by an uppercase letter (like 'camelCase') and inserts a hyphen between them (turning it into 'camel-Case').
explanations.52: normalize('NFD') breaks accented characters into their base letter plus diacritics separately, then the next line removes those diacritics so 'café' becomes 'cafe'.
explanations.62: If the post's frontmatter has a custom slug field, use it; otherwise derive the slug from the folder structure.
explanations.87: We're calculating the path of the translation file that would correspond to this English blog post—same folder structure, but under the i18n directory instead.
explanations.89: If a translated version of this post exists, use that file's content instead of the English version so the mirror and index show translated titles and body text.
explanations.99: path.relative() gets the folder path relative to blog/, split() breaks it on path separators, then join('/') reassembles it using forward slashes (so Windows backslashes become normal slashes).
explanations.130: We're normalizing the baseUrl to always end with a slash so we can safely concatenate it with other path segments without accidentally creating double slashes or missing slashes.
explanations.142: If date is a Date object (which the YAML parser creates), slice the ISO string to get just the YYYY-MM-DD part; otherwise convert it to a string as-is.
explanations.215: The spread operator converts the Map's values (which is an iterator) into an array, then sort() arranges posts alphabetically by title.
explanations.242: new Date(a.date) - new Date(b.date) returns a negative, zero, or positive number, which sort() uses to order the posts from oldest to newest.
explanations.264: We extract the current locale name from the i18n config passed by Docusaurus, falling back gracefully if it doesn't exist.
explanations.266: Boolean() converts the condition to true only if we have a currentLocale AND it's not the same as the default locale—this tells us we're building a non-English version.
explanations.288: collectTranslations() returns an object mapping locale names to sets of slugs that have been translated; we get the slugs for the current locale or an empty array if none exist.
explanations.292: We extract the slug from the post's permalink using a regex (the part between '/blog/' and the trailing slash), then check if that slug was actually translated into this locale.
explanations.312: This function normalizes a bare permalink into the full path including the locale's baseUrl, so `/blog/foo` becomes `/fr/blog/foo` for French builds.
explanations.315: We strip trailing slashes from all the live routes Docusaurus generated, then store them in a Set for fast O(1) lookup when filtering posts.
explanations.336: unknownComponents is a list of custom React components the MDX-to-Markdown converter couldn't fully convert; we collect all of them to warn the developer later.
explanations.348: We construct the output file path by taking the post's permalink (like '/blog/my-post') and appending '.md', then converting it to a real file system path under outDir.
explanations.352: Only posts that are not marked draft and not marked unlisted get added to the searchable index—everything else gets mirrored but hidden from the llms.txt catalog.
